finding: CLASS-I-SEASONAL-CYCLIC-CASCADE. Simard 1997 + Gorzelak 2015: Douglas-fir transfers C to paper birch; birch later transfers C back at different time of year when Douglas-fir under increasing shade. THIS IS bi-directional seasonal cyclic-cascade Class I (cyclic-group Z/n) where n ~ 365 days and cascade-orientation (Class C) reverses every half-cycle. C_flow(t) = orient(L_CMN, gradient(t)); gradient(t) = gradient_amplitude(t) * sign(cos(2*pi*t/365)). Composed I o C describes seasonal phenology cleanly. Class I canonical primitive: cyclic-group Z/n modular arithmetic; srmech_zn_* C primitive v0.4.0rc1 shipped. Substrate-specific implementation: deciduous-coniferous photosynthesis phase-offset.

finding: CASCADE-SHAPE-SURVIVES-MAGNITUDE-DISPUTE. Karst Jones Hoeksema 2023 (Nature Ecology and Evolution 7:501-511 PMID 36782032 cite-by-ref via Nature TOS) found three of four big CMN claims INSUFFICIENTLY SUPPORTED: (a) CMNs widespread in forests (results vary too widely; alternative explanations); (b) Resources transferred via CMNs increase seedling performance (same); (c) Mature trees preferentially send resources + defence signals to offspring (no peer-reviewed evidence). Klein et al. 2023 PMC10751480 affirms transfer is real but small / nuanced (osmoregulation + defence metabolite transfer, not bulk growth; 0-10% C; 0-72% N range across studies). Framework verdict: this is a MAGNITUDE-CRITIQUE not a CASCADE-SHAPE-CRITIQUE. Per [[user_stance_framework_domain_algebra_not_length_or_magnitude]] cascade-shape is magnitude-free. Cascade L+M+C+K+I is present-as-operations in substrate regardless of whether operations transmit 0.1% or 10% of plant carbon budget. The dispute does not falsify cascade-shape attestation.
